Planar slices through a gridded scalar field

Source: R/layers-stats-volumes.R
stat_slice_3d.Rd

Cuts a complete rectilinear x/y/z grid with a numeric value aesthetic by planes and colours each section by the field, as MATLAB's slice, plotly's isosurface slices and PyVista's slice() do. Each plane is sampled on a lattice of points and the field is interpolated trilinearly within its grid cell. A plane perpendicular to an axis (xslice, yslice, zslice, or a slice plane with an axis normal) is sampled on the grid's own coordinates along the two other axes, so a slice on a grid layer reproduces the grid values exactly; any other plane is sampled on n x n points over the rectangle around its section with the grid box, and the lattice triangles are clipped to that section. Triangles with a missing corner value are dropped. With no slice given, one slice per axis passes through the centre of the grid, as in PyVista's slice_orthogonal().

Usage

stat_slice_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomStatsSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  xslice = NULL,
  yslice = NULL,
  zslice = NULL,
  slice = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_slice_3d(...)

stat_density_slice_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomStatsSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  h = NULL,
  adjust = 1,
  n = 32L,
  xslice = NULL,
  yslice = NULL,
  zslice = NULL,
  slice = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_density_slice_3d(...)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

geom

Geom prototype for keyed triangle corners.

xslice, yslice, zslice

Positions of planes perpendicular to the x, y and z axes, in transformed position coordinates.

slice

NULL, a plane made with sdf_plane(), or a list of them, for slices in any direction.

n

Lattice size per side for oblique planes; NULL uses the largest grid dimension. For stat_density_slice_3d() the density grid resolution, which also sets the lattice.

h

Positive bandwidth, scalar or one per axis; NULL estimates it.

adjust

Positive automatic bandwidth multiplier, scalar or one per axis.

Details

Computed variables: value, the mean of the three corner values of each triangle (fill is constant per face), and slice, a factor naming the plane ("x = 0.5", "plane 1"). The default fill is after_stat(value). Slices are not shaded; pass shade = TRUE to light them.

stat_density_slice_3d() slices the Gaussian product-kernel density of stat_density_3d(), computed on its n grid; density is the computed density.

References

MathWorks. slice: Volume slice planes. https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/ref/slice.html

PyVista. DataObjectFilters.slice_orthogonal. https://docs.pyvista.org/api/core/_autosummary/pyvista.dataobjectfilters.slice_orthogonal

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12),
                 y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12), z = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12))
d$value <- with(d, exp(-(x^2 + 2 * y^2 + z^2)))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, value = value)) +
  geom_slice_3d() + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, value = value)) +
  stat_slice_3d(slice = sdf_plane(c(1, -1, 1)), n = 30) + coord_3d()
set.seed(1)
p <- data.frame(x = rnorm(200), y = rnorm(200), z = rnorm(200))
ggplot2::ggplot(p, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_density_slice_3d(zslice = 0, n = 24) + coord_3d()
